text: Dori'thur is the large, snowy spirit owl companion of Tyrande Whisperwind.
Dr. Morrigan is a banshee who works for . She specializes in harvesting souls in a study she calls Soulology!

For the other related groups see Man'ari, Lightforged draenei, Broken, Lost One. The draenei (meaning Exiled Ones in their own tongue) are a faction of uncorrupted eredar who fled their homeworld of Argus to escape the corruption of the demonic Burning Legion. Led by the Prophet Velen and guided by the divine naaru, they traveled throughout the cosmos in search of a safe world to settle on, eventually landing on a planet they would come to call Draenor, or "Exiles' Refuge". For centuries, the draenei lived in relative peace with Draenor's native orcs, until agents of the Burning Legion found them. As the orcs were corrupted by the Legion and formed the original Horde, the draenei were slaughtered en masse and driven into hiding. Decades later, the survivors managed to escape the ravaged world of Outland aboard the Exodar, a vessel of the naaru fortress Tempest Keep, but crashed upon the world of Azeroth; more specifically, on the Azuremyst Isles off the western coast of Kalimdor. Inspired by tales of the heroic Alliance that stood against the might of the Burning Legion during the Third War, the draenei joined their ranks and led the charge during the Invasion of Outland. Following the defeat of Kil'jaeden at the Sunwell Plateau, the draenei completed the desperate mission that first brought them to Azeroth, and some of them were sent back to Outland to revitalize their former civilization. However, the majority vowed to stay and uphold their sacred commitment to the Alliance

The is a melee weapon featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 6. It is only available in the Campaign. The Clawhammer can be found in the mission Most Wanted on the floor outside of the black site's door and in High Rollers, and can be used as a standalone melee weapon as well as being used for takedowns even when it is stowed.

The dracthyr are an ancient race of humanoid dragonkin. They have the ability to wield the magic of all five primary dragonflights as evokers, and, like true dragons, shapeshift between a draconic form and a humanoid visage. The dracthyr were created in the ancient past at Aberrus by the black Dragon Aspect Neltharion, who combined the essence of dragons with the adaptability of the mortal races to create a race of ideal soldiers. Neltharion fashioned the Forbidden Reach off the coast of the Dragon Isles to serve as the dracthyr soldiers' training ground, but after a terrible battle against the Primalists, Neltharion put the dracthyr into a slumber that lasted. Recently, the Primalists' return caused the dracthyr to stir, and they now seek to forge their own path in Azeroth by joining both the Alliance and the Horde. The dracthyr are divided into armies known as weyrns, each led by a Scalecommander. Scalecommander Azurathel and the Obsidian Warders joined the Alliance, while Scalecommander Cindrethresh and the Dark Talons joined the Horde. Scalecommander Viridia and the Healing Wings traveled to the Dragon Isles, while Scalecommander Sarkareth and the Ebon Scales defected from the dracthyr army after feeling abandoned by Neltharion and renamed themselves the Sundered Flame. Scalecommander Emberthal's Adamant Vigil was wiped out by the Primalists, and she remained in the Forbidden Reach to search for answers.

A dragonman is a type of dragonkin. Maloriak was a human kidnapped by Nefarian and fused with the corpse of a dragonspawn. The result was a bumbling minion who possessed only a dull of his former intelligence. Failed fusions are called aberrations and can be found in the Fleshrender's Workshop. Several of them appear as enemies in Island Expeditions, accompanying the black dragonflight.

For encounter details, see Dread Ship Vazuvius Dread Captain Genest is the ghostly skeletal captain of the Dread Ship Vazuvius. He is buried at the Cursed Gravestone in the Misty Strand on Timeless Isle, but can be called forth using a Mist-Filled Spirit Lantern. The Time-Worn Journal implies that he and his crew (and possibly the ship itself) were devoured by Evermaw before becoming ghostly pirates.

The Charge Amp PV is a Barrel attachment available uniquely for the EX1 Assault Rifle in Call of Duty: Vanguard. It allows the EX1 to function as a high damage "railgun" style weapon by charging up a shot to full power, which is indicated by the turbine spinning, before this high power shot can be fired. A shot can be fired at any charge level, albeit at a much reduced damage level. Charging the EX1 also is classified as firing the weapon.
Dread Captain Vandegrim is a human ghost located in Freehold.

Dreadweaver Avartu is a mogu ghost found in the Ruins of Korune in Kun-Lai Summit. Long ago, he was present when Shan Kien hid the Divine Bell. Instead of retreating with their workers and warriors, Shan Kien left them in the ruins and kicked Avartu back as well.

__NOTOC__ Dregmar Runebrand, a male magnataur runemaster. He lives in a cave in Dragonblight and ventures out of it only to survey the landscape. His cave is strewn with the bodies of animals, some only half-eaten, suggesting a huge appetite. Confronting him is required for the quest Reclusive Runemaster. As a Rare Elite, Dregmar Runebrand patrols near the Ruby Dragonshrine in The Deaths of Chromie. Upon death drops Sands of Time.

Coaxial Machine Gun is a vehicle perk in Call of Duty: World at War which allows the driver to fire a forward mounted machine gun, granting the tank driver a considerably greater anti-infantry capability. The machine gun fires at head level in whichever direction the body of the tank is facing, so although the range of motion is limited, it is much more effective against infantry than the tank's main turret, and does not require the driver to switch seats for machine gun access. When the main gun of the tank is facing forward, the player is able to aim the machine gun with the crosshairs. This perk is unlocked at level 40.
Dresaelus is a kyrian commemorated in the Ancient Memorial in Bastion which blesses anyone who touches it. He invented single use glider.
Dreamkeeper Y'sani is a green dragonspawn located at Algeth'ar Academy in Thaldraszus.
Dreamgrove Hippogryph is a hippogryph located in Ashamane's Gate in Val'sharah during the The Shrine of Ashamane questline.

Cold Feet is the sixteenth and final level of Call of Duty: Black Ops (Nintendo DS), where the player must destroy a Soviet submarine that will be used to deliver Nova 6 to the United States. The player must then evacuate the facility before the explosives detonate and destroy the facility.
Dreamguard Taelyasra is a wylderdrake located in the Ohn'ahran Plains.
Autumnal Baskin was a professional meditator and a bare-knuckle champion.

The Argonians are the reptiloid natives of the Black Marsh of southern Tamriel. Their amphibious physique suits them for aquatic and terrestrial habitation. Years of living in dangerous bogs and swamps has bolstered their immunity to the diseases and poisons found there. Behind expressionless faces, Argonians possess a quiet intellect, and because of this, many are talented mages. Naturally agile, Argonians also make keen rogues and warriors.

The Combat Knife is a melee weapon featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops II, Call of Duty Online, Call of Duty: Ghosts, Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare, Call of Duty: Black Ops III, Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare, Call of Duty: WWII, Call of Duty: Black Ops 4, Call of Duty: Mobile, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, as well as making a brief appearance in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 Campaign Remastered.

Falmer Spellsword are a type of Falmer that dwells in the ancient Dwemer Ruins and caves across . They are blind, but possess an extremely sensitive hearing and will investigate even the slightest noise. They usually carry a Falmer War Axe, and can use Healing and Frostbite.

Lieutenant Fazumir is a Khajiit boss residing in the southeastern corner of Rimmen Necropolis in . She uses shadow magic to attack. She can also create a clone of herself in addition to summoning a large shadowy hand, which may kill the Vestige outright if not avoided.

Wild Witch is a generic character located in any Alliance zone in . They can be found dueling a Sorcerer or Cryomancer with a fire staff and will teleport away if they win. They can be interrupted during the duel and killed.

:For similar weapons, see Axe, Tomahawk, Hell's Retriever and Throwing Knife. The is a variant of the Tomahawk used in Call of Duty: Black Ops II, Call of Duty: Black Ops III, Call of Duty: Black Ops 4, Call of Duty: Mobile, Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 and Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. It can also be seen in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III.

Zurin Arctus, sometimes referred to as Master Arctus, was the first Imperial Battlemage and Grand Vizier of the Septim Empire during the late Second and early Third Era, as well as a former overseer of the Imperial City until the throne was taken by Tiber Septim. It has been said that the Morag Tong assassin Dram was an apprentice of Arctus. Zurin Arctus was known to be an astounding tactician as well as an accomplished diplomat and intellectual. His magical skill was unmatched by any other mage of his time, which may be attributed to his believed connections to Magnus, the god of magic. Arctus is typically regarded as the Underking, though his identity is sometimes contested with Ysmir Wulfharth.

Honored War Beasts are a the common Elite variant of the Cabal War Beast. Honored War Beasts are more durable and aggressive then the regular ones. In the Red Legion, they differ from their standard counterparts by their heavier, silver-colored armor and higher durability. Shadow Legion Honored War Beasts instead have gold armor rather than purple, and a darker coloration then their regular brethren. Like standard War Beasts, they are feral, vicious attack animals deployed as either shock troops, a distraction, or as cannon fodder to protect their other forces. They are quick, highly aggressive, and very tenacious, stopping at nothing until either they or their enemies are dead.

Monzaemon X is a Puppet Digimon and carrier of the X-Antibody. The love overflowing from within its body has manifested as a Lovely Gel that is filled with hearts, and its cuteness has gone up even more. It is happy to pluck its Lovely Gel and give it to Digimon drawn in by its cuteness. Since the Digimon that receive it feel happy, it seems that it likes watching them smile more than anything. Should an enemy appear that attacks the Digimon who have gathered together, it will repel them with its "Hearts Splash". Attacks *Hearts Attack (Lovely Attack): Flings hearts. *Hearts Splash (Lovely Splash): Pours large amounts of its Lovely Gel over the enemy. This technique becomes more powerful as the support for Monzaemon increases.

The Comics Camouflage is a weapon camouflage skin that is set to appear in Call of Duty: Black Ops II. It was part of the Comics Pack, but since the pack lost during the voting period on all platforms, the camouflage was unobtainable. The pack was revitalized when it was released much later on April 30th, 2014.

ZombiePlutomon is an Undead Digimon. With the functions of its DigiCore halted, Plutomon—a Digimon that typically enjoys a long life—has become a strange being whose body is simply going through the motions. It no longer possesses any free will, nor does it punish evil, having lost its sense of purpose too. Cursed by its undying DigiCore to wander endlessly, it can no longer contemplate anything but the indiscriminate consumption of others' data. A fearsome predator in a completely different sense when it was alive, ZombiePlutomon's decaying flesh ensures that its hunger will never be sated, no matter how many DigiCores it devours. Attacks *Hazard Hold: Absorbs data from its prey's DigiCore until they decay. *Hell Slicer: Launches sickle-shaped from its left hand to carve up enemies. * Abomination: Bites foes and infects them with its own virus, turning them into puppets it can manipulate.

The clawfoot is a two-legged dinosaur, with sharp teeth and a single toe claw that looks like a small sickle. It is no larger than a tall human, but looks like it could easily take down much larger prey. Like their cousins the carvers and great carvers, clawfoots bring down their prey with their speed and their talons. In the wild, clawfoots use pack tactics to hunt their prey.
Caliphear the Nightmare was a black horse with flames for her mane and tail living on Corondor.
Cobweb is a weapon camouflage skin featured in Call of Duty Online.

Dashing Thief Sparkla, referred to as Masque the Dashing Thief on two occasions in The Perfect Infiltration, is a Sparkla Theet in Princess Peach: Showtime! He is initially trapped in the basement of the Sparkle Theater by Grape. After clearing The Stolen Statue (in which the titular golden statue of himself is stolen by the Sour Thieves), Princess Peach and Stella have the opportunity to rescue the Dashing Thief Sparkla in the stage The Dark Prison & the Dangerous Trap. In the aforementioned stage, the Dashing Thief Sparkla is trapped in a cage, so Dashing Thief Peach must unlock four locks scattered in different areas. After all locks are deactivated, the Dashing Thief Sparkla is released, but the place starts falling apart, therefore both dashing thieves must escape. After unlocking more locks and ziplining, both dashing thieves use hang gliders to fly to the exit. After clearing the stage, the Dashing Thief Sparkla can be found on the second floor of the Sparkle Theater, where he is admired by other Theets. Before the final battle against Grape, all of the Sparklas, including the Dashing Thief Sparkla, give Princess Peach Sparkle Power to allow her to transform into Radiant Peach. All of the Sparklas are then seen in the ending, where they celebrate with everyone.

The Mutant Ninja Sentai Nokonokoman are a group of original enemies that briefly appear in two chapters of the Super Mario-kun manga. They are a parody of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles from the , preceding the Koopa Bros., another parody of the Ninja Turtles from Paper Mario, by ten years. They are formed by four masked Koopa Troopas, each one with a shell of a different color: red, blue, green, and yellow. They first appear in chapter 13 of volume 1, where they impede Mario, Luigi and Yoshi's path by disguising themselves as an extendable Warp Pipe. After Mario realizes that the pipe is not an inanimate object, the four Koopas present themselves and then proceed to attack the trio with Kamenoko Shurikens that hit Yoshi. Mario and Luigi try to attack them, but they use another disguise trick and all of them transform into four Princess Peaches. Mario and Luigi, although knowing it is a trick, are too lost to fight them, but then notice that all the princesses have a shell on their backs. Mario defeats them with a cape twirl and the heroes continue on their trip. In the second chapter of volume 2, one of the Koopas is seen being punished by Bowser, who is stomping him, a Chargin' Chuck, and a normal Koopa Troopa under his feet in anger for his minions' many failures.

Clarence Whistler (February 24, 1856 - November 6, 1885) was a professional athlete and champion Greco-Roman wrestler of the 1880s. As the main rival to William Muldoon in wrestling of the early 80s, he was best remembered for his unusual strength, indifference to pain and tragic death. He wrestled three famous bouts with Muldoon, totaling over 14 hours.
The Competitor Weapon Kit is a Bounty weapon kit available in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered.
Yo Senkai (楊占海 Yang Zhanhai) is a character from Street Fighter II V. He is an old master of Chinese martial arts and medicine.

and a Blue Jellyfish and mining blocks alongside the player. Note how it can double jump while mid-air to reach its target.]] Cattiva is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Cattiva minion. It runs and jumps towards enemies, dealing contact damage. When Cattiva is falling and its target is more than 6.25 tiles above it, it can also perform a double jump with visuals similar to the Cloud in a Bottle to reach its target. Unlike the double jumps used by the player, Cattiva does not need to land on the ground to refresh its double jump and can use it endlessly while mid-air. Cattiva can also mine alongside the player with a pickaxe power equivalent to 41% (approximately that of the Iron Pickaxe) and mining speed of 16. It will continue to mine even after the player stops, as long as the player is still nearby. Cattiva will also cut down trees and cacti alongside the player, either cutting the same tree/cactus or another one nearby. It has an axe power of 171% when cutting trees and an axe power of 57% when cutting cacti, as well as a chopping speed of 16 in both cases. Only one copy of Cattiva can be summoned at a time; additional uses of the summon weapon do not summon additional minions, nor do they improve the existing minion. Like other Pals, Cattiva can be petted using . Cattiva has a rare chance to spawn on Grass, Jungle grass, Snow, or Ice blocks above surface during daytime if the player is not in a Graveyard biome, but it cannot spawn in the center 1/4 of the worl

The Elves were the fairest creatures in Arda, a far more beautiful race than Men, and generally tall (seldom less than six feet for elf women, no less than six and a half feet for elfmen). Among them, those who had gone to Valinor were the fairest and had the greatest skill of body. Elves had keener senses than Men. They were graceful yet strong, and were resistant to extremes of nature, illness and disease. However, many Noldor died at the crossings of Helcaraxë. Practical considerations, including a number of occasions where Men were mistaken for Elves (most notably Túrin Turambar), suggest that the points of difference between Elves and Men must have been subtle.
The Cordite is a submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 4 and Call of Duty: Mobile.

__NOTOC__ Captain Alennah Starsong was a night elf captain of the Sentinels slain at Astranaar in Ashenvale by Lorash during the War of the Thorns. Her body was found by Captain Delaryn Summermoon. As of Dragonflight, she can be seen floating around as a wisp in the city of Bel'Amath, Amirdrassil.

Ice Toads make their appearance in "What is Life?" They stand guard in front of the Ice King's room and make an alarm (literally shouting "ALARM!") if there are intruders. It is possible that their alarm summons the Ice Bull.

The Marshmallow Kids are six delinquent marshmallows that live in the Candy Kingdom. They first appear in the episode "Susan Strong" when they refuse to run away from the Hyooman tribe, stating that "The Marshmallow Kids never run from a scrap!" and Jake then accidentally sets them on fire as they run to fight. This sets the Hyooman tribe's hats on fire which makes them rip them off, revealing they aren't human before fleeing. The Marshmallow Kids then shed their burnt skin. When Finn asks if they'll be alright, they reply that they'll just be gooey for a while. One of the kids can be seen again in "Mystery Train", Five Short Graybles" and "Candy Streets," with a female one appearing in "Bad Little Boy." The Marshmallow Kids play a major role in "Scamps," where a gang of four of them—Gary, Johnny, Sunshine, and Hugo—are caught by Finn and Jake trying to scam Starchy. After learning of their underprivileged street background, Finn takes them on a camping trip in the wilderness to try to show them about life beyond scamming. They grow to respect him and as of the end of the episode, they appear to be attending the Candy Kingdom Preschool.

Cold War Remedy is an Easter Egg for the map Classified, in which the Ultimis crew must locate and retrieve the Project Skadi weapon prototype. It is also the Easter Egg for acquiring a free Winter's Howl within Classified.
* H'dang Li, a newborn foundling babe, is placed into the care of the lamas of Tabot. The child develops magical powers and a keen intellect.

*Govan Irfandel uses his affinity with the plants, vines, trees, and wildlife of the impenetrable Brush of Barbs to build the druidic Stone Circle of Govan. The circle was intended to be the meeting space, shelter, and ritual site for goodly druids. ;Novels * Chapter 1 of Vampire of the Mists

* In Silverhand Tower outside Neverwinter, Alassra Silverhand is born to Dornal Silverhand and Elué Shundar through the intervention of the goddess Mystra. She is the sixth of the Seven Sisters, mortal servants of the goddess. She would later be known as Simbul and the Witch-Queen of Aglarond.
The Compact Scope is an optical attachment for the Mozu revolver, the Daemon 3XB submachine gun, and the Reaver C86 crossbow in Call of Duty: Black Ops 4.

Abinor Lashingwind was the patriarch of a family of storm giants who lived with them in the highest peak of the Gnollwatch Mountains in the mid–14th century DR. He did all he could to keep his family secret from both the human and Crinti who lived in the lands surrounding the mountains in Dambrath. To this end, circa 1372 DR, he created the illusion of a moody silver dragon in the peaks to ward off any explorers or errant monsters.
Abrians were intelligent ostrich-like creatures who dwelt in the Abyss and other sparsely populated regions of the Outer Planes. They traveled in flocks and had supernatural shrieks.
Aataqah was a djinni captured by the cruel mage named Jon Irenicus circa 1369 DR.
Compagnie Generale Sevier is a weapon manufacturer in Call of Duty: Mobile.
Aeron Morieth was a half-elven wizard and shadow adept who lived in Chessenta.

Aesperus, also known as the King in Copper, was a lich wizard dwelling near the city of Hulburg on the Moonsea. Aesperus was known as "the King in Copper" because of the enchanted copper bands he wore on his body.
Aghul Balai was a member of the Tsu-tsu tribe of the Plain of Horses in the mid–14 century DR. He was a follower and Chung Tao of the Way.

The Conversion-Ready Binary Repeater-Standard, shortened as the CRBR-S (Cerberus), is a wonder weapon featured in the Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War Zombies map Mauer der Toten. It also makes a cameo appearance in the Zombies reveal for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III.
Aganazzar, or Aganazzar of Neverwinter, sometimes spelled Agannazar, was a renowned wizard of The Covenant and founder of Neverwinter's School of Wizardry.
Adriyana Voudsarr was the Magister from to . Mystra transformed her into Adriyana's Garter at her request.

Aglarra Galdekund is the wife of the merchant Flammos Galdekund of Waterdeep. In 1369 DR, Queen Filfaeril Obarskyr assumed her appearance in order to hide in Waterdeep during the abraxus affair. The change in mannerisms and voice was blamed on an illness, that the couple had to travel to Iritue's Firesprings in southern Amn in order to address. Aglarra is short and masculine in appearance, with a pot belly and a large, pimpled chin.
The is an assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Vanguard. It was added as part of the Season One update.
Ak'chazars were a breed of deadly rakshasa necromancers. They possessed the typical rakshasa desire to dominate and extended their reach to mastery over the dead.
Alaia Serrat was a powerful human shaman and one of the three leaders of the merchant family House Serrat. She was the adopted mother of the yuan-ti pureblood Zaltys Serrat.
Aihonen was a great hero who killed the white dragon Icasaracht.
Compressed Rounds is an ammo type available exclusively for the Cooper Carbine in Call of Duty: Vanguard. It helps to increase the gun's fire rate but at a cost of the accuracy.
Al-jahar, or dazzles, were sinister creatures found in Zakhara, the Land of Fate, who masqueraded as beautiful humanoids.
Ahskahala Durothil was a legendary dragonrider in Evermeet in 1367 DR.
Alathrien Druanna was a minor elven goddess of rune and conjuration magic. She was a nearly-forgotten member of the Seldarine, as most elves practicing magic called upon Corellon Larethian for aid.

Concussive Ammo is an ammunition type available exclusively for the Gorenko Anti-Tank Rifle in Call of Duty: Vanguard. It adds a suppression round that stuns enemies if fired near them. If a player has Dauntless, this has no effect.
Alai was an arcane spellcaster who dedicated himself to the dogma of the Iron Throne leader Sarevok during the mid−14 century DR.

An Ching Wang was a kensai of the town of Cham Fau in the Ch'ing Tung province of Shou Lung and later a member of the Emperor's guard in the spelljammer spaceport city of Chunming in the mid–14 century DR.
Amon was a mage who adventured along with several companions in Amn during the mid–14 century DR. He was seemingly a member of the enigmatic Purple Brotherhood.
The Coil Amp is a muzzle attachment available uniquely for the EX1 assault rifle in Call of Duty: Vanguard. It helps to increase the damage but at the cost of the damage range.
Argularragh was a dragon who lived in the realm of Eskorn, Laerakond, in the centuries before the Spellplague.
Asenath was a powerful sorceress and former slave who went on a lifelong war against the Red Wizards of Thay long before the 14 century DR.

Aruph "Red" Thunderfist was a red-haired, burly fence from Luskan. A man who could always get the best deal on just about any item a person could want, Red was well-liked and respected all over the city. He could often be found conducting business in a corner booth in the Cutlass, where he downed an endless number of drinks with near immunity to the effects of intoxication. Red was never one to betray the trust and was often willing to accept favor over gold as payment for his services.

The Comms Plate Carrier is an equipment featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II and Call of Duty: Warzone 2.0 added with the Season Three update. It could originally be found with the DMZ mode. In Warzone 2.0, it was added to Battle Royale, Resurgence and Plunder with the Season Four Reloaded update. That update added a two-plate version of the Comms Plate Carrier to both games. When equipped, the vest functions like the Bird's-Eye perk and a signal booster which allows for an increase in duration of UAVs, UAV Towers and enemy radios. When these are active, they will function as an Advanced UAV. The player will also receive a communication from the announcer, which will change depending on the amount of players nearby: *The announcer will simply say there are enemy operators nearby if a single operator or two operators are nearby *The announcer will refer to any group of operators with 3 members as a squad of operators *The announcer will refer to a group with 4 or more members as a platoon of operators.

The aurumvorax (; ), sometimes known as the golden gorger, was a small, shaggy hole-dwelling creature with eight legs that was able to eat gold. It was sometimes used to locate gold, being able to detect and find its veins in the ground. It was not fearful and could become vicious, able to defend itself against formidable creatures like chimerae.

Augathra the Mad was a Netherese magic user, scholar, and seer. She received visions and wrote them down into a chronology that would become known as the Roll of Years. To her chagrin, she received dark and disturbing visions during her sleep. These disturbing visions would become known as the Black Chronology and she would pen them into a new tome now called the Book of the Black.
Aulagol was an illithilich wizard and a member of the Concord of Elders that governed the illithid city of Ch'Chitl in the Northdark of the Underdark in the mid–14 century DR.

The Compression Carrier is a Vest featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III. It was added as part of the Season Three update. The Compression Carrier allows the player to have faster health regeneration immediately after getting a kill or capturing an objective. The player will also resist enemy tacticals, and in some cases, are completely immune. When equipped with the Compression Carrier, the player is only allowed to carry one Lethal, Gloves, Boots and Gear.
Aurin, better known as Aurin the Generous, was a businessman and accomplished conjurer who lived in Skullport in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

Aulstaer Mrelgaunt was a scholar of the Art of such skill that he retained his spellcasting abilities after becoming a ghost. In his afterlife, he haunted his tower in the foothills of the Nether Mountains known as Mrelgaunt's Turret.

Auziiyra Twelvestars was a human mage of Tethyr. Alongside Brondeth of the Broken Staff and several other mages, Auziiyra was guarding a human mining community when they were attacked by drow. The mages used the wonderform spell to hide in the form of wingless wonders and escape being killed, but became lost in the Underdark. They were thought to still be wandering the Night Below by the mid–14 century DR.

The Cooper 21" Scythe is a Barrel attachment available exclusively to the BAR Assault Rifle in Call of Duty: Vanguard. It increases the long range abilities of the BAR by increasing both the bullet velocity and the damage range by a substantial amount with a minor increase to the aiming speed. This comes at the cost of a heavy increase to the recoil.
Aylen Attricus was a powerful wizard who helped found the city of Tantras in the Vast.

Baerduin Thask was a human magic-user and a member of the adventuring company known as The Four. His fellow members Telorn, Fiirfar Nulomn, and Diloule "Lanternhand" were all hanged as assassins in Tethyr on the day before Higharvestide in 1369 DR following the siege of Myratma. Baerduin would have faced a similar end but he escaped justice by leaping off the seaside cliffs overlooking the ruins of Ithalyr, laughing as he did so. Not even the sea elves ever found his body and his fate remains unknown. Among his other crimes, Baerduin Thask was responsible for transforming prisoners into Broken Ones, bestial and misshapen combinations of humans and animals created as a result of scientific or magical experiments gone wrong.
Avorals were eagle-like guardinals that lived in Elysium and the House of Nature. Of all the guardinals, they were the most likely to leave their homeplane, as they possessed a strong wanderlust.

Colt can refer to: *Colt M1911, a pistol in most games of the series. *Colt M16A1, an assault rifle in Call of Duty: Black Ops (Nintendo DS), Call of Duty: Black Ops Mobile, and Call of Duty: Black Ops II. *.44 Magnum, a revolver in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, Call of Duty Online and Call of Duty: Ghosts, in some cases referred to as "Colt Anaconda" in the game files. *Python, a revolver in Call of Duty: Black Ops and Call of Duty: Black Ops II, referred to as "Colt Python .357 Magnum" in the Black Ops guidebook *CM901, an assault rifle in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 that has the Colt logo on its side.
Azdraka was a green dragon who was slain by Lady Tanamere Alagondar and several adventurers in the late 14 century DR.
Baelric was Firefingers' doorman as of , during the Rage of Dragons. He was present in the discussion of Mirtul 20. He was a brawny man.
Azmyrandyr of the Twelve Talons, was a Red Wizard of Thay in the mid-14 century DR.
The is a British cruiser tank used during the events of Call of Duty 2 in the North African theater.
Balder (), sometimes spelled Baldur or Baldr, was an interloper god of beauty and charisma from the multi-spheric Norse pantheon and who was believed by some to be a dead power.
Banana Candy was a well-trained hadrosaurus who competed in the dinosaur races of Port Nyanzaru in Chult during the late 15 century DR.
Baneliches were liches who served as clerics of Bane during their mortal lives.

The DEVGRU Camouflage is a weapon camouflage skin that is introduced in Call of Duty: Black Ops II. It closely resembles the Multicam Camouflage from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3. It is the first camo to be unlocked on all weapons. If applied to the SCAR-H on the campaign with a reflex sight attached, it will cause it to turn white, unlike in multiplayer where is remains dark grey.
Batalista was a grand mage and the creator of the enchanted ring known as Batalista's Passport.
Behrshimmer was an emerald dragon wyrm who lived in the Giant's Run Mountains in the 14 century DR.
Basa Lianin was a noblewoman, patrician illusionist, a landowner, and a merchant from Bral in the mid–14 century DR.
Cyborg Camouflage is a type of weapon camouflage skin featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops II and Call of Duty: Black Ops III.
Bay was a werewolf from Moray in the Moonshae Isles during the late 15 century DR.

Beau was the pseudodragon familiar bonded to Methrammar Aerasumé, a wizard and fighter who served as the Argent Legion's High Marshal, by the late 14 century DR. The two were inseparable, with Beau often accompanying his master into danger. Luckily, the tiny dragon-kin was typically protected by Methrammar's spells and a magic item that Beau kept in his possession.
Berg'inyon Baenre was a drow weapon master of House Baenre of Menzoberranzan in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
The Crocodile Camouflage is a weapon camouflage skin featured in Call of Duty: Ghosts.
Belisarius is a powerful mage, who resides in Carradoon, at the foot of the Snowflake Mountains.

Belmer of the Six Thunders was a local archwizard of Calimshan. As of , he was working as a "firestop" mage on a roadside inn, "The Vizier Vanquished". He was the last one to die in the Night of Fourteen Magisters.
Berchtwald Bandyleg was a human shaman of the Uthgardt Elk tribe in the Savage Frontier in the mid-to-late 14 century DR. He venerated the Elk totem of Uthgar at the Flint Rock ancestral mound.

The Cyborg Doomsday Warship is an airship featured as a boss in the Cyborg Evacuation and Air Reaper modes of Call of Duty Online. It appears after all survivors have been evacuated. In Air Reaper, UFOs can generate a force shield around the warship, preventing players from damaging it while still allowing the warship to fire its energy missiles.

Black dragons, also known as skull dragons, were far and away the most vile-tempered and cruel of all chromatic dragons. They were solitary creatures that lived in the swamps and marshlands all around Toril, from the Flooded Forest in Sembia to the jungles of Chult.
Big Old Red was a large and powerful werewolf with red fur that roamed the King's Forest of Cormyr during the mid-1480s DR.

Blaskar Lauthlon was a male human wizard, and the Overwizard of the Host Tower of the Arcane and Master of the West Tower. He was responsible for the Arcane Brotherhood's operations in the western quadrant of Faerûn.
Creature Camouflage is a weapon camouflage in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare. It is available with the purchase of the Creature Pack.

Blooden was a succubus and mistress of the Deep Crest, the breeding grounds of the Abyss. She was one of the demons and devils bound to Ammon Jerro in order to increase his warlock power. She appeared to have an infatuation with Koraboros, despite the fact he was devil and she was a demon. She commented rather casually that she had mated with many mortal men, even those of celestial descent, but none had survived her violent mating habits.

The Blood-Curdling Scream was a rock gnome vampire illusionist and priest of Urdlen of the 14 century DR. The Blood-Curdling Scream led the Blood Screamers, a savage pack of dire weremole gnomes who made their lair in the Bandit Wastes of Lapaliiya and launched raids from the Nathaghal Mountains and all the way to the Nath in Halruaa and to the Rathgaunt Hills at the end of the Channath Vale in the Shaar.
Bladuid was an elder gold elf high mage from Evermeet that served as the aide to Lord Laerm Ryence, co-commander of the Swift Cavalry as of the late 14 century DR.

Customized Weapon is a feature in Call of Duty Online. It is a special variant of regular weapon equipped with integrated camouflage and attachments, which can’t be unloaded by players. However, its camouflage can be replaced if other camouflages are available. Parts of the Customized Weapons are not customizable, but they are usually attached with two or more attachments by default.
Bloodeye was a werewolf and leader among the lycanthropes of the Black Blood tribe on the island of Moray in the Moonshae Isles during the late 15 century DR.
Bok was a powerful flesh golem manufactured by Dendybar the Mottled, a wizard and the guardian of the northern spire in the Hosttower of the Arcane in the seaport city of Luskan.
Mama Booga was an orc bandit and shaman of the Clotskull orc tribe in the 15 century DR.

The DMR-1 (known as DMR-M1 in early builds, and as M1 in the game files) is a sniper rifle that appears in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. It resembles an M1 Garand which has been adapted for use as a marksman rifle by the addition of a lengthened barrel and an offset scope. It can also be reloaded mid-magazine, unlike the M1. Upon close inspection, one can see a flaw in the wooden stock under the rear sight, possibly a knot in the tree the stock was carved from, but more likely a crack from extended periods of use by soldiers with enhanced strength due to their combat rigs.
Bookas were an uncommon race of small, sprite-like fey. They were most closely related to sprites and pixies.
Boggarts, sometimes called "boggies", were the immature forms of will-o'-wisps who often took the form of a small humanoid via their shapeshifting abilities.
Blunt Skuncher was an evoker mage thug who opposed the The Guild crime gang of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
The D13 Sector is a secondary weapon featured as a special weapon in Call of Duty: Black Ops III and Call of Duty: Black Ops 6, and as a launcher in Call of Duty: Mobile.
Boraksaghegirak, commonly called Borak, was an ancient blue dragon residing in the ruins of the city of Imer in the Calim Desert.
Brandon ( ), nicknamed "Battlemaster", was a human fighter and a renowned sword-for-hire around the Sea of Fallen Stars in the mid–14 century DR.
Buckweather, also known as Sprite-Heels, was a halfling thief and Lord of the Watch of Ankhapur on the Lake of Steam in the late 14 century DR and a former member of Pinch's thieves guild.
The DIY 11 Renovator is a fully-automatic nail gun featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops III. It appears as a submachine gun, added in the October 17th, 2016‎ update.
Broargar "Windcloak" Iringil was a Impilturan wizard and instructor of the Art who lived in the city of Lyrabar during the 14 century DR.
Briel, known as the Archmage Briel, was a human wizard of the 14 century DR.

Calimar Arkhenneld was a drow lich enchanter of the city of Sshamath in the 14 century DR. He was the Master Emeritus of the School of Enchantment and Charm, as well as a former member of the ruling Conclave of Sshamath.
The D-8 Cleaver is a Jackal-mounted weapon featured in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare.
Calabastasingavor was a blue dragon who lived in Threskel. He was a servant of Alasklerbanbastos.

Caalenfaire was a powerful elven diviner of ancient Myth Drannor obsessed with knowledge of the secrets of past and the future who unwillingly became undead bound to one of the vaults inside the Speculum. He guided the heroes from Phlan, the Veiled Ones, on their quest to stop the nefarious plans of the Cult of the Dragon in 1369 DR.
The Calavarr was a powerful wizard who once ruled the city of Tulmon in the Land of the Lions region of south Faerûn.
Creeper is a Common Gun Perk that appears in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare, found upon certain weapon variants. It increases movement speed while crouching.

Calagrace was a minor mage, and the mother of Irithra Dawntanthra. She fled her native Calimshan for the islands in the Moonshaes to avoid an arranged marriage. She died at some point before of a winter fever; before then, she scried extensively.
Burlmarr was a gnomish inhabitant of Ieirithymbul in the mid-to-late 14 century DR. He had budding psionic powers.
Centiv Naomal was a human wizard specializing in illusions in Waterdeep in the late 15 century DR.

The D-25S (referred to as DMR25 in the game files) is a semi-automatic sniper rifle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered. It was added in the March 14th, 2017 update.. It is available for use after the player completes the D-25S collection in the Depot. Once unlocked, the D-25S is available for use at all levels. The D-25S can be equipped with an ACOG Scope after achieving 100 kills with it.
Chaney was the name assigned to a doppelganger who was Howard Holiday's chief spy in Ravens Bluff around 1356–1357 DR. No one knew its real name, or if it even had one.
Cedra was a yuan-ti half-breed leader and sorceress who allied with the Legion of the Chimera.
Cellayne was a powerful necromancer affiliated with the Zhentarim in the mid–14 century DR.

The Counter Recon Aircraft is a Scorestreak featured in Call of Duty: WWII. It is visually based on the P-61 Black Widow. The Counter Recon Aircraft functions differently compared to how the Counter-UAV and Counter-Spy Plane streaks worked in previous games. Instead of scrambling the mini-map, it will pursue and engage an enemy Recon Aircraft or Counter Recon Aircraft, destroying them. If called in without any enemy Recon Aircrafts in the air, it will fly over the map and block any new enemy Recon Aircrafts from being called in during it’s 30 second duration.

Chant Morven was a portly human pawnbroker with a shop in one of Airspur's seedier districts. In spite of his large size, he was unusually nimble and quick on his feet. Chant owed a large gambling debt to Raneger, a local crime lord.

Chathin Zurn was the khazark of the enclave of Thay within the city of Proskur in central Faerûn during the late 14 century DR. As the highest-ranked Red Wizard within the city, she had the full authority of Thay within the city. Chiathin was a champion of the strategy to establish enclaves within cities near the Inner Sea, and voraciously debated this view against the standpoint that Thay should outright conquer other nations.
Charmaine was the favorite servant of Szass Tam, the powerful lich and Zulkir of Necromancy of Thay, in the mid–14 century DR.

Cross Bar is an operator mod in Call of Duty: Black Ops 4 and an attachment in Call of Duty: Mobile, exclusively available to the Hades light machine gun. It reappears in Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 as an attachment.
Charas of Winterwood was a renowned invoker from the Lake of Steam region, active in the 2 century DR.

Daelegoth Orndeir was a fire genasi cleric of Amaunator, evangelist, and sunmaster from Elversult in the mid–14 century DR. He was the leader of the Brotherhood of the Glorious Sun and a believer in the Risen Sun heresy, which claimed Lathander to be Amaunator's reincarnation and furthermore that the Morninglord's re-transformation into the Yellow God was nigh.

Cynda was a halfling ranger and the twin sister of Shan. She was also an accomplished aerialist in the Circus of Wonders. Her voice was damaged in a fight with an undead creature and she lost her ability to speak. Shan communicated with her sister using sign language.
The DL Q33 is a bolt-action sniper rifle featured in Call of Duty: Mobile.
Cymmarraa was a wizard between the late 14 and late 15 centuries DR. Going by the moniker "Lady of Ghosts", she pursued a grudge against Elminster and Manshoon both.

Daethleness Tuin'Tarl was a drow wizard of House Tuin'Tarl in Menzoberranzan, active some time before the mid–14 century DR. In order to escape Lolth's justice, Daethleness used the wonderform spell to hide in the form of a wingless wonder.
Daggermaw was a large, old, and notably aggressive hunter shark in the Sea of Swords along the Sword Coast North as of the late 15 century DR.

Corvus Defense, abbreviated as CD is a weapon manufacturer in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Mobile, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III, Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Their logo is their name Corvus Defense in all caps with a crosshair centered between the C and O of Corvus; "Defense" is rendered in much smaller font on a second line below "Corvus".
Cyrel was a wizard and a trader that operated out of a tollhouse situated along the Risen Road within the Sword Coast region during the late 15 century DR.
Czszudleaux was a powerful gnome illusionist inhabiting the city of Daggerford in the Western Heartlands during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Dalanyrr was a young silver dragon that dwelled in the North during the late 15 century DR.

Cronen Tactical is a weapon manufacturer in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Mobile, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III. Their logo is simply a large, blocky capital C.
A cursed imp was a rare variant of the common imp, imbued with magic capable of spreading poison and disease.
Cyrvisnea was an ogre mage who attacked the southern cities of Amn in West Faerûn.
Danica Bonaduce, formerly known as Danica Maupoissant, was a human monk from Westgate who settled at the Edificant Library in the mid–14 century DR.
The Cronen Sniper Elite is a grip tape attachment featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare. It is uniquely available to the Grau 5.56 assault rifle.

Darlan Morten was a male half-elf shadow adept who was one of the members of the Shadow Council of the Shadow Thieves. Darlan was an obscure manipulator of the Shadow Weave who used his position to increase his collection of magic items. His duty was to control the guild's operations between Baldur's Gate and Amn.

A darklight was an undead creature of the Quasi-Elemental Plane of Radiance. Mortal spirits that departed their bodies at death, but did not become petitioners and then became lost on their way to its final rest, might arrive at the Plane of Radiance. Here, they were filled with radiant energy and became free-willed undead beings, called darklights. They appeared as humanoid-shaped specters of blackness with bright, shining eyes of ever-changing colors.

The Dark Urge was the name given to a white dragonborn Bhaalspawn sorcerer—and the chosen of Bhaal―who lived in the Realms during the late 15 century DR. The name referred to the murderous and violent urges he received during many events he encountered in his life.

The is an aircraft featured in Call of Duty: Vanguard. The plane appears during the Campaign mission Numa Numa Trail where it is used by Wade Jackson and Mateo Hernandez to escape and later assist the in eliminating the Japanese forces.
Dalyria was a vampire spawn and one of the favorite "children" of the vampire lord Cazador Szarr, who resided in the Szarr Palace of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Deceiver genies were tasked djinn whose lives revolved around deception and illusion. Oddly enough, deceiver genies were more susceptible to believing illusions than most creatures.
Davy Jones, born Reinhold William Rauschpautton, was a wizard in the city of Ravens Bluff who operated a storage facility known as the Lock-Up.

Cowabunga Camouflage is a weapon camouflage featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered. Like the Friends Forever Camouflage, it was added to the game as part of the Days of Summer event and could be unlocked by completing a certain set of challenges. The challenges include winning 10 matches (Assault Rifles), calling in 10 UAVs (Submachine Guns), flashing 25 enemies (Light Machine Guns), killing 10 enemies with frag grenades (Shotguns), killing 50 enemies overall (Sniper Rifles) or by killing 10 enemies with a melee weapon (Pistols). The camouflage appears as a blue and white wave in the ocean.
Darthym was a War Wizard of Cormyr in the late 14 century DR.

Dasumia, known as the Lady of Shadows, was a malevolent, Banite sorceress in the mid–8 century DR. She took over Galadorna and was served by the apprentice mage Elminster Aumar, a Chosen of Mystra, but ultimately revealed herself to be an avatar of Mystra herself.
Grand Arcanist Darstil Vurusk was a powerful wizard and senior officer of the Night Brigade gang in Wheloon Prison in Cormyr in the late 15 century DR.

The DIM X-Circuit Battery is a Magazine attachment available exclusively for the EX1 Assault Rifle in Call of Duty: Vanguard. It helps to improve the damage range and aim down sight speed but at the cost of the fire rate.
Lord High Justiciar Deren Eriach was an inhabitant of the Abbey of the Just Hammer. On 22 Mirtul 1373 DR, Eriach killed the green dragon Sirvinhandra who had attacked the abbey.
Deidre Kendrick was a wizard and cleric of Talos of the Moonshae Isles in the mid–14 century DR.
Deljasaa Rammathor, whose nickname was Lady Wind, was a rogue inhabiting Waterdeep, City of Splendors, during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

The [https://modernfirearms.net/en/assault-rifles/u-s-a-assault-rifles/ngsw-r-gd-rm277-2/ Cronen Squall] is a bullpup weapon that appears as a battle rifle in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III, and as an assault rifle in Call of Duty: Mobile and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

Delainy was a werewolf who lived in the werewolf village on the Isle of Balduran in the Trackless Sea in the mid-to-late 14 century DR. Gorion's Ward encountered her when he and his party were shipwrecked on this island.
Devamari () was a doppelganger criminal in Mulmaster in 1491 DR.

Dhalmass Obarskyr, known as the Warrior King, was a king of Cormyr from 1210 DR to 1227 DR. He was the sole heir of Pryntaler Obarskyr and the father of Palaghard II. He was remembered in history for reconquering Marsember.
The is a marksman rifle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III.
Dimwold was a fire mephit in the service of Orcus in the Abyss in 1357 DR.
Diakka (), also sometimes known as diakkas (), were avian creatures native to all the layers of the plane known as Hades.
Dire badgers, also known as giant badgers, were bigger, tougher, smarter cousins of regular badgers. There were known to be animal companions of rangers, druids, and gnome cavaliers.
The is a bullpup assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 6. It was added as part of the Season Two update.
Destrin Chamaerlyn, who was also called the Sword of Tyr, was a paladin of Tyr inhabiting Urmlaspyr in 1358 DR.
Diogi the Wanderer was a human wu jen from T'u Lung, Kara-Tur, in the mid–14 century DR.
Dhaunryl Zalimbar was a mage inhabiting the city of Waterdeep during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
The Cut-Off Stock is an attachment in Call of Duty: Black Ops 6. It is a Stock attachment and is unique to the Essex Model 07 Marksman Rifle.
Dondon was an afflicted wererat halfling in Calimport with many underworld dealings.

Doric was a tiefling druid and a member of the Emerald Enclave based in the Neverwinter Wood in the late 15 century DR. Born to human parents, Doric spent much of her life living among a community of wood elves of the North, before embarking on a series of adventures that would take her to the lands south of Waterdeep, to the city of Neverwinter, and even the perilous Underdark. She was a fellow adventurer of Edgin Darvis, Holga Kilgore, and Simon Aumar.
Dolly Dolly Dolly was a pixie trapped inside a moonlantern carried by drider Kar'niss of the Absolute in the late 15 century DR.

The DIM Uproot Short is a Barrel attachment available uniquely for the EX1 Assault Rifle in Call of Duty: Vanguard. It increases the close range handling of the EX1 alongside removing the charge-up time that it suffers from. However, this comes at the cost of a slight reduction of the capacity alongside an increase in recoil and reduction in the effective range of the beam.

Dmitra Flass, also known unofficially as the First Princess of Thay or The Tharchioness, was the Tharchion of Eltabbar within the realm of Thay during the mid-to-late 14 century DR, and subsequently the Zulkir of Illusion among the Red Wizards during the War of the Zulkirs. She was also a powerful figure in Mulmaster following her marriage to that city state's ruler, High Blade Selfaril Uoumdolphin.

Dorn Il-Khan was a half-orc blackguard who traveled across west Faerûn seeking vengeance during the mid–14 century DR. Hailing from the Spine of the World, Dorn spent many years operating as a bandit in Luskan, before being double crossed by his colleagues and left for dead. His anger at this betrayal attracted the attention of the demon Ur-Gothoz, who restored and empowered Dorn with demonic abilities, in return for his service.
Doth was a dwarven mystic and member of the Dancing Dwarves in Zakhara in 1367 DR.

The D50 Radar Flatbed is a vehicle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 where it is available in the DMZ mode. When being driven, a UAV will be activated for all players inside the vehicle, functioning like a UAV Tower.
Draethren Tanthul was one of the Princes of Shade and the best sorcerer of Thultanthar.

Dornal Silverhand was a human ranger who lived in the 8 century DR and most notably fathered the Seven Sisters with Mystra while she possessed the body of his wife, Elué Shundar, in a dramatic series of events that led to her death at his hands. Enraged, Dornal scoured the North for twenty years until meeting his death in battle, being granted relief by the Goddess of Magic and continuing his existence as a being known as the Watcher.
Driders were drow that had been transformed from the waist down so they had the body of a spider. The transformation was typically a punishment for failing a test of Lolth.

DMR may refer to: *Marksman Rifle, also known as DMR (Designated Marksman Rifle) - A weapon class in various games. *DMR-1 - A sniper rifle in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. *Auger DMR - A tactical rifle in Call of Duty: Black Ops 4. *DMR 14 - The M14 rifle as it is called in Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War.
Dragonspawn, also known as the spawn of Tiamat, were a type of creatures descended from true dragons. They were the antithesis of the dragonborn of Bahamut.
Duhlark Kolat () was a powerful mage and inventor of spells who lived in Waterdeep.

Druhallen was a particularly talented mage that traveled the Western Heartlands during the mid–14 century DR. He famously ventured into the mines of Dekanter along with his old flame Rozt'a, her foster son Tiep, and a particularly well-mannered goblin to save the life of his longtime friend Galimer, and wound up recovering an ancient artifact from the lost empire of Netheril.

Commander David Welsh, callsign Fox Three, was a British Crusader Tank Commander who fought German armor units during World War II. Welsh is a playable character in the British campaign of Call of Duty 2.
Drejjd was a doppelganger inhabiting Waterdeep during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Drauthtar Inskirl was a Zhentarim veteran mage in the mid-14 century DR.

Elué Shundar, also known as the Lady of the Gate, was a female half-elf sorcerer and adventuress who shared her body with Mystra. The goddess' possession enabled Elué to give birth to the Seven Sisters, all of Mystra's Chosen and fathered by the Elué's husband, Dornal Silverhand.

The Degtyarev DP-28, also known as the DP27, is a Russian light machine gun that appears in Call of Duty: United Offensive, Call of Duty: Finest Hour, Call of Duty: World at War, Call of Duty: Vanguard and Call of Duty: Mobile. It can be easily identified by its unusual pan magazine and the distinctive stuttering sound it makes when firing.

Elgred Morbide was a dragonborn lich sorcerer and necromancer who was a follower of the dracolich An'Kizhek. He attacked the Dungeon Academy and stole the keystone of the Nexus Marker, which protected the school.
Fennis was a tasked winemaker genie who served the Brotherhood of the True Flame in the fortress of Krak al-Niraan in 1367 DR.

A Fang of Yeenoghu was a gnoll that had been been possessed by a demonic spirit, a gift bestowed upon them by the demon lord Yeenoghu. They were considered the Lord of Savagery's most favored servants.

The is a secret weapon and base for all weapons, which appears in every Call of Duty game based on Infinity Ward's Quake 3 engine branch. It can only be obtained via console commands on PC or hacking on consoles.

Fierna was the lady of Phlegethos who, along with Belial, her father, were the only archdevils allowed to share rulership over one of the Nine Hells by Asmodeus. In their peculiar partnership, Fierna was the young newcomer with fiery passion and undoubtable appeal.
Ferrix, also known as the Lady of Weretigresses and often portrayed in myth as Mother Tigress, was the goddess of female weretigers.
Fi Lendicol was a silver dragon in the Stonelands during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

A damage multiplier is the number that the base damage of a weapon or attack is multiplied by to yield the actual damage. Although the values of the numbers have changed throughout the series, generally shots to the head and neck increase damage, while hitting the limbs and hands will decrease damage. A damage multiplier is featured in every Call of Duty game to date and determines how in-game damage is distributed to the body. The higher the multiplier, the more lethal the shot.
Flapjack was a flumph sailor and adventurer who traveled Wildspace in the late 15 century DR.
The Founder, also known as the Red Woman, was a Red Wizard of Thay in the late 14 century DR.
Fonmara was a duergar mind master and a cultist of the Absolute that dwelled in the ruins of Grymforge for a time during the late 15 century DR.

The DShK (Degtyaryova-Shpagina Krupnokaliberny, Degtyaryov-Shpagin Large-Calibre) is a Russian Heavy Machine Gun. It is often referred to as the "Dushka", meaning "dear" or "sweetie" in Russian. It is seen in Call of Duty: Black Ops, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, Call of Duty: Black Ops II, Call of Duty: Ghosts, Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare, Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War, Call of Duty: Mobile and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III.
Fulminorax was a blue dragon allied with Valindra Shadowmantle in 1484 DR.

Fremlins were a type of winged gremlin that didn't originate on the Material Plane. Their original plane of existence was unknown, but it was speculated that they had been brought to the Material Plane as a result of careless conjuration.

Gadacros were lesser tanar'ri demons that induced blindness in their prey and savored the taste of freshly plucked eyes. They were the carrion crows of the Abyss, appearing in the wake of death and disaster to harry and victimize the survivors.
Damage is a shotgun-exclusive Weapon Proficiency in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3.
Fylanthalas was allegedly a great mage who lived sometime before 1372 DR.

The Blightfather is a special Zombie in Call of Duty: Black Ops 4 Zombies mode on the maps IX, Voyage of Despair, and Ancient Evil. It also spawns in Zombies locations in the Blackout mode, as well as the Specialist HQ mission for Katsumi "Recon" Kimura. It returns in Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War on the map Dead Ops Arcade 3: Rise of the Mamaback.

The Dark Assassin is an enemy featured in the Darkness Infiltration game mode in Call of Duty: Mobile as part of the collab with . Dark Assassins are equipped with the Poltergeist cloaking devices and wield an M4.
The DSR 50 is a bullpup, bolt-action Sniper Rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops II.

Petty Officer First Class Enhanced Tactical Humanoid 3rd Revision (E3N) (A.K.A. Ethan) is the tritagonist in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. E3N is designed to be a "one-of-a-kind" tactical soldier bot capable of human responses and emotions, making him significantly more advanced than standard C6 robots, which are little more than mindless drones. Initially, he is not accepted by some of the crew members, especially Omar, though even Omar grows to appreciate him over time. Ethan appears in Call of Duty: Siege as the guide to the player. He helps teach the player the controls and gives a tutorial of the game. Ethan is also featured as a playable character in Call of Duty: Mobile and was added during Season 1: New Order as part of the "Firewall Crate".

Doctor Peter Glücksbringer Straub was the main antagonist and a character that appeared in the Nazi Zombies mode of Call of Duty: WWII. He was the creator of the undead, creating and augmenting this new army with the use of a special energy.

Riley is a dog featured in Call of Duty: Ghosts and in the comics of Call of Duty: Mobile. He is a member of the Ghosts squadron; Riley is part of the player's team and works as a friendly character who will help and support the player by "sniffing out explosives and assisting the player against hostiles." He can be remotely controlled by the player during certain points of the campaign. He is also able to take down helicopters by jumping up and biting the pilot if they are close to the ground. He incurred a non-lethal bullet wound to his left thigh in Sin City, and survived when Logan loaded him into a helicopter at the end of the mission. Although healed, Riley is last seen in the prologue of All or Nothing.

The DTSRS is a sniper rifle cut from Call of Duty: Black Ops II. A big and small menu selection image can be found in the game files. They are named, menu_mp_weapons_dtsrs_big and menu_mp_weapons_dtsrs, respectively.
Skating Divas, also known as Roller Skaters, are a Zombie type that appear in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare Zombies mode on the map Shaolin Shuffle.
Abracadaniel is an Uncommon ally in Bloons Adventure Time TD. He turns bloons into butterflies at a slow rate (acts somewhat like the Bloon Master Alchemist). He costs $580 to place.

Gumbald (for more information, see Gumbald) is a Super Rare Ally in Bloons Adventure Time TD, introduced in Version 1.5.0. He shoots damaging chemicals at bloons that stun them for a short time, along with 1 damage. He can only be equipped to Princess Bubblegum, Warrior Bubblegum, Finn, Dungeon Finn, Max, Juggernaut Max, Captain Cassie, Commander Cassie, Supermonkey, and Ice King. He costs $530 to place.

Lieutenant David Walker (codenamed: Hesh) is the non-playable deuteragonist of Call of Duty: Ghosts. He is Logan's older brother and Elias' son, as well as Riley's caretaker. He joined up with U.S. special forces alongside his brother and father following the ODIN strikes in California to serve in the Federation War.
Ice Monkey is a playable character and exclusive to Bloons Super Monkey 2 Mobile. He is unlocked after completing all the Monkey Lane stages.

The Ninja Monkey is a monkey that made its first appearance in Bloons TD 5, appearing in every Bloons game, except Bloons Adventure Time TD, released since. Its purpose as a base tower is having default camo detection making it useful against early Camo Rounds. In tower defense games, it throws shurikens that pop a few bloons each. In Bloons Pop!, it glides through the air swiping at bloons with karate moves.
Peter I (9 June 1672 – 8 February 1725), also known as Peter the Great, was Tsar of the Russian Empire from 1682 until his death. He leads the Russians in Civilization IV.
The Dead Man's Hand Camouflage is a DLC weapon camouflage skin available for Call of Duty: Black Ops II. It is available for anyone who buys the Dead Man's Hand Pack.

Rani Lakshmibai is an Great General in Civilization VI. Her unit provides +5 Combat Strength and +1 to Industrial and Modern era land units within 2 s. Rani Lakshmibai can be retired to instantly create a unit with 1 level.

Marcus Ulpius Trajanus (18 September 53 – 8 August 117), more commonly known as Trajan, was emperor of Rome from 98 AD until his death. He is best remembered for achieving one of the greatest military expansions in Roman history, as well as for his philanthropic rule, enacting extensive public building programs and welfare policies that led to him being recognized as one of the "Five Good Emperors". He leads the Romans in Civilization VI. Rome is the one civ you can trust to continue to push to be the largest empire in the game. Trajan takes Julius Caesar's words to heart: "Veni, vidi, vici" (I came, I saw, I conquered).

Adanrel is a Bosmer rogue who lives with Methredhel in the Imperial City's Waterfront District. Unlike her roommates, Adanrel has few skills and is not a member of the Thieves Guild. She is exceedingly poor and is discouraged by that fact. She spends all of her time in the Waterfront District. If she is not walking around or in her house, she is at the Bloated Float. She may be found working in one of the Imperial Trading Company Warehouses from 9 AM to 6 PM. She wears lower-class attire consisting of a dark green shirt, laced leather pants and stitched leather shoes. She also carries the key to Methredhel's house and a meager amount of gold. In combat, she relies on an iron bow, an iron dagger, and either a Chameleon, Invisibility or Silence spell.

Deathbringer is a Rare gun perk in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare, found upon certain weapon variants. It refills the magazine upon the achievement of a double kill. When a double kill is scored with a weapon that has this perk, its magazine is instantly refilled. This does not deplete the reserve stored ammunition stocks, and can be achieved without needing to obtain both kills with the same weapon for Deathbringer to activate; as long as it is equipped for the second kill, the magazine will be refilled. In Zombies, Deathbringer activates after a quadruple kill instead of a double kill.
Addut-Lamanu is a Dunmer Ashlander healer who resides at her yurt in Erabenimsun Camp, in the Molag Amur region.

The Afflicted are humanoid races who have been gifted abilities or "afflicted" by the Daedric Prince, Peryite, in Skyrim. Afflicted have the ability to vomit a green substance that is extremely acidic. It appears that Peryite "afflicted" them so that they could "cleanse all of Tamriel" by spreading this affliction. They can be found in the Dwemer ruins of Bthardamz, due west of Dragontooth Crater. After completing Peryite's quest, a group of Afflicted may hunt the Dragonborn (under the name "Remnants of Afflicted") similar to how a Hired Thug would be paid to do so if the Dragonborn had severely angered or wronged a character.
